questions.q: In Deuteronomy 5:15, what reason is given for Israel keeping the Sabbath?
options: Because farming needed a day off
Because the priests demanded it
Because they had been slaves in Egypt and were now free to stop
Because rest was a reward for finishing the week's work
questions.explanation: A people who had never been allowed to stop were commanded to stop. As the chapter puts it, a person who cannot stop is not free, however productive they look.

questions.q: According to Luke 5:15–16, what did Jesus do as the crowds and demands grew?
options: He worked longer hours to meet the need
He withdrew once, in a crisis, and never again
He sent the disciples away and stayed with the crowds
He withdrew to desolate places and prayed, as a repeated habit
questions.explanation: The demand went up and his response was to withdraw more, not less. The verb form describes repeated, customary action: this was his rhythm, not a one-off.

questions.q: What is the difference the chapter draws between running away and retreating?
options: Running away has no intention of returning; a retreat is a withdrawal in order to return
Retreating is longer than running away
Running away is for the weak; retreating is for the strong
There is no real difference
questions.explanation: Jesus went to the desolate place and came back to the crowd. A retreat exists so you can go back to your family, work and church with something to give again.

questions.q: How does the chapter contrast Jonah and Elijah, who both fled?
options: Jonah was forgiven; Elijah was not
Jonah fled in resistance to God's word; Elijah fled in fear but remained responsive to God and received his direction
Both were rebuked for leaving their posts
Elijah fled to Tarshish; Jonah went to the wilderness
questions.explanation: Jonah went 'away from the presence of the LORD' (Jonah 1:3). Elijah ran in fear (1 Kings 19:3), yet ate what God provided, went to Horeb and answered God honestly. The test is whether you turn toward God once you get there.

questions.q: Which sentence does the chapter call the most dangerous of the three lies that keep people from resting?
options: "If I stop, everything will fall apart."
"Other people have it harder, so I have no right to be tired."
"I will rest once this season is over."
"Rest is only for people whose lives are easy."
questions.explanation: The season rarely ends on its own; one deadline replaces another. Elijah did not choose to stop, he collapsed. It is better to choose.

questions.q: What does the chapter say about your responsibilities before you take a retreat?
options: They should be abandoned; the retreat comes first
Nothing needs arranging because God will take care of it
Only single people without dependants should take retreats
Essential responsibilities should be delegated, simplified or arranged for, not abandoned; preparation is itself an act of responsibility
questions.explanation: Preparation is different from postponement. Explain what you need, arrange care for those who depend on you, and use an adapted format if three full days are genuinely impossible.

reflection: Which of the three sentences above sounds most like you? Write it out in your own words.
Who would be affected by you taking three days away? Now write, honestly, how they are affected by the version of you that never stops.
Jonah fled in resistance to God. Elijah fled in fear, then turned toward God. If you are honest, which direction are you facing right now, and what would it take to turn?
What must be arranged, delegated, postponed, or explained so that you can enter this retreat responsibly and without unnecessary distraction?
